You might also consider how to handle characters that aren't part of the data you actually want.

Since this is for a live assessment, I cannot validate whether a specific sequence of methods will work for your problem. I suggest you try running that logic with a test case in your local environment to see if the resulting list contains the strings you expect.

I can certainly show you a general example of type conversion. If you have a list like `['1', '2', '3']` and want to convert it to a tuple of integers, you could use a generator expression inside the `tuple()` constructor. For example: `tuple(int(x) for x in my_list)`. This pattern is useful whenever you need to apply a transformation to every element in a collection.
Okay, so I combine the cleaning, the splitting, and that generator thing. I think I've got it now. Thanks.
You're welcome. Applying those concepts in sequence is a solid approach to string parsing. Good luck with the rest of your quiz!
